accept: Driving the staple needs lever. Folding the legs on the anvil is wedge. Folding the legs as its own lesson (wedge) instead of a sub-function of the drive is acceptable.
A spring that lifts the arm back up is an acceptable third sub-function of the drive, and may be left out.
Feeding the next staple is a lesson answered by spring.

The base, the rubber foot and the staple channel are givens. An opening top for reloading is a welcome given but not required, since the scan does not show it. The rubber foot as a grip lesson is wrong.
Feed comes after the drive, because its gap only shows on the second press.

plan.job: Pins sheets of paper together with a bent wire staple.
uses: Press again on the next stack.
Open it and drop in a new strip.

mechanisms.name: Base
mechanisms.does: Sits steady on the desk and holds the paper.

mechanisms.name: Staple channel
mechanisms.does: Holds a row of staples in line.

mechanisms.name: Staple drive
mechanisms.does: Punches one staple through the paper and folds it flat.

gap.try: Push a staple through a stack of paper with your thumb.
gap.fails: The legs buckle and nothing holds the sheets together.

subfunctions.does: Turn a hand press into a hard, straight push
Fold the legs flat under the paper
Lift the arm back up for the next press

mechanisms.name: Staple feed
mechanisms.does: Brings the next staple under the blade by itself.

gap.try: Press the arm a second time.
gap.fails: Nothing comes out, because no staple is under the blade.

subfunctions.does: Push the strip forward as each staple leaves

mechanisms.name: Opening top
mechanisms.does: Swings open so a new strip can be dropped in.
